english_verification.review_scope: Checked the current Mod's A55 identity, 1444 history, Menibór localisation, the two A55-specific Luna missions, A55 national ideas, the shared Luna mission context, and successor B59 idea terminology. Read the related Luna River and Pírluna River Wiki chunks. This is not an exhaustive audit of every mission, event, formation condition, or B59 route.
english_verification.shared_text_integration: The primary read the native B59 appendix, Curtain Call tooltip and Pashainé formation block while assembling the shared article; these are bounded integration checks, not a full successor mission audit.
unresolved: The dedicated Free City of Menibór Wiki pages are present in the local corpus (page 774) but were not read in this bounded check; wiki_status remains related_only.
The Luna River and Pírluna River pages provide geographic and city context, not proof of A55-specific current mechanics.
The source article's shared narrative, maps, score table, and B59 formation details are handled in the shared article by the primary agent; this overlay preserves only A55 text fields.
The inherited source descriptions and effect displays are translated faithfully; current Mod scripts were checked for terminology, but no source-data or unit correction was made.

rationale.campaign_length: A55 has 20 visible shared Luna missions and 2 country-specific missions; forming B59 switches to a separate mission tree.
rationale.colonization: The A55 Luna prelude is not aimed at overseas colonisation; H48's adventurer overseas route is a separate switchable Tag.
rationale.complexity: Resource menus, estate agendas, the Emperor's relations, subject attitudes, and the formable-country threshold run in parallel.
rationale.dark_story: This article focuses on the trauma of war, autonomy, and political calculation rather than systemic atrocities; B59's later story is not back-projected.
rationale.difficulty: The difficulty lies in political resources and alliance management, including the pacing of some trade and city missions.
rationale.diplomacy: Sway, Imperial favour, city attitudes, and allied subjects form the daily operational core.
rationale.early_pressure: A one-province start is wedged among larger imperial princes and must rely on diplomacy and mercenaries for protection.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Anti-magic amulets belong to the city's history and ideas; A55's main gameplay is not spellcasting or artificery.
rationale.narrative_density: The trauma of the Lilac Wars, Free City autonomy, the adventurer tradition, and the shared Purple River identity form a continuous prelude.
rationale.tall_play: The specific missions require capital development, while the valley-wide route emphasizes industry, art, universities, and urban growth.
rationale.trade_economy: River transport, trade privileges, the capital market, urban commerce, and alliance tariffs are important themes.
rationale.warfare: War is still needed to liberate or control Luna cities, but Imperial politics and subjects matter more than continuous conquest.

identity.appearance: A Republican Free City in the Empire of Anbennar in 1444; one of the four Luna countries listed in the scoring table.
identity.region: Luna River / East Dameshead / Empire of Anbennar

successors.relationship: The final shared Luna mission unlocks the formation conditions; the decision changes the Tag and switches to a country-specific mission tree.

survey_region.note: Shared source row: Luna River Minors (Rank 3; Region EoA). The original table aggregates the four local Luna countries; this mapping does not claim that they are one EU4 country.

national_ideas.scope_note: Country traditions, seven national ideas, and ambition only; optional idea groups and species/government bonuses are excluded. Multiple candidates and conditions are listed separately and are not treated as simultaneous; whether the new ideas are accepted on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: Menibór is second only to Anbenncóst itself in terms of how many adventurers hail from our city. From Derwing to Aiscestir, hopeful heroes of the Eastern Dameshead and beyond flock to our inns and taverns to begin their lives as adventurers, forming powerful and prestigious companies such as the Menibór Free Company in the process.
description.text_en: Menibór is second only to Anbenncóst itself in terms of how many adventurers hail from our city. From Derwing to Aiscestir, hopeful heroes of the Eastern Dameshead and beyond flock to our inns and taverns to begin their lives as adventurers, forming powerful and prestigious companies such as the Menibór Free Company in the process.

description.text: During the Wars of Rule, the Magisters of Oldtower and the knights of Valiant Keep frequently clashed near our city, their magics risking the integrity of our walls on several occasions. To deal with them, small anti-magic wards were created to be mounted on the walls and worn by our warriors, allowing them to properly defend Menibór from the arcane chaos spreading around her.

description.text:
Nothing soothes a tired adventurer more than a serving of Bridgewine with a hefty sausage!

Known more professionally as simply 'Menibór', it is a moderately strong red wine that is known for its spicy notes and high acidity - and has found strong favor amongst the bolder characters of Cannor.

description.text: Ever since the fall of the Damerian Republic our city has been one that few can manage to hold onto for long. Several times Damerian and Vernman forces alike were banished from the city by the adventurer companies and embroiled in bloody wars to reclaim her. Even though we've settled into the Empire, our neighbors know well the lengths a Menibórian will go to for our continued autonomous status.

description.text: The Loop is the most famed tavern in the Luna Basin, only catering to the most legendary heroes, who frequently gather there to discuss happenings and glories abroad. The proprietors of the establishment are quick to inform us of anything of note that they hear, always ensuring the reach of our city council remains in The Loop.

description.text: The dwarves of the Riverstone Clan were hired long ago to construct the many bridges that cross the Luna in our city, and they stayed behind to maintain them. As the city grew around their homes and workshops they expanded their influence, constructing virtually every structure in Menibór and operating as the city's primary architects and engineers to this day.

description.text: The dream of every adventurer from Menibór is to have their statues and names featured in the hallowed corridors of the Hall of the Gallant, a vast memorial dedicated to those heroes that lost their lives fighting for glory and justice. With names and busts dating back to before the Dragonwake, it is the most well known and respected edifice in the city.

“The greatest rulers preside not over a mere reign but an Era, a period which eclipses those ahead and behind in its profundity and prolificity. They understand that the legacy of the patron is his clients.”
Tomás of Vallusna, ‘The Statesman’

description.text:
“The imitation of style necessitates the imitation of form, and therefore of function. When we build a colonnade inspired by the formal markets of Old Dameria, we are inspired also by the conversation held along that colonnade, the type of life enabled by the structure we seek to recreate. The rhetorical tradition, the vibrant public life, even the raucous protest – all are made possible by the decision, made once again, to build space for them.”
Saman of Fowlbarn, ‘The Life Of Stone’

description.text:
“Even in those realms which had not subordinated their government to an association of guild-backed aldermen, the Guild had been the fundamental unit of urban life in the Eastern Dameshead long before Pashainé’s emergence as a coherent state.

This had three major consequences. First, the codification of a sort of corporate democracy, a belief that society was best forged under a competing set of mutually-exerted pressures, by groups representing collectives of the population - even if these were subject to a monarch or a so-called ’Executive Guild’. Second, an emphasis on economic prosperity, the brass tacks ‘shopkeeper diplomacy’ for which Pashainé became notorious. Third, a relentless focus on urbanisation and the vertical integration of industry.”
Silvard Dove, ‘An Economic History of Cannor’

description.text:
“The poet Milian said that the Pashainéy is uniquely noble, having inherited the bravery of his Vernman father and the dignity of his Damerian mother. As a second daughter, I seem to have been left with the libido and stubbornness.”
Genaia ‘Geni’ Cadesna sina Bellacaire, ‘Memoirs Of A Fallen Countess’

description.text:
“Consider the conflict between Corinism and the Court which had so split the Valley. Consider, then, an unusually literate and engaged populace with a political impetus to see theological ruptures healed. Consider finally the Ravelian Lodge, which in its structure mimics the voluntary association basis of the guild. No population on Halann was more ready to embrace not merely the articles of belief but the basic organisational structure of Ravelianism.”
Leande Bellac, ‘Apologetics’

description.text:
“Over the course of the eighteenth century, the slowly aggregating impact of the Verdancy became more and more clear across the entire Luna watershed. Land which had once been among the most fertile in Cannor gave harvest perhaps once in two years, while the concomitant soil pollution devastated the Valley’s few remaining natural forests. The result was an exodus of the population from the countryside and an even greater urbanisation of Pashainé, inadvertently birthing a contentious café and street culture; this would dominate the labour politics of the following hundred years, erupting again and again into civil unrest. You will find few along the Valley who have much to say in praise of Camir Silmuna, but our land is indelibly marked by his legacy.”
Lucas síl Bellacaire, The History of the Lilac River, Vol. II

description.text:
“Do not fear death, my people. Fear nothing which you do in the company of brave souls; fear nothing which you do among your fellow citizens! We live in the time of the Mage-Emperors – in the era of the staff – and its power seems absolute. But we know these mages can die.

We knew it three hundred years ago, when the discipline of the fusillade first began to rival the arc of the fireball. We knew it two hundred years ago, when first we learned of that glorious substance, then accessible only so very far away, which could countermand their unearned gifts. And we know it now – now that their ritual of growth, their promise of endless harvest, has wrought a desolate steppe where once there was only verdant life. It is what they do! Addle the land, poison the water, wreck the bountiful Halann we share for the slightest chance at a lonely throne.

Hear me! It’s true – we may die today. But we die together, while they die alone.”
Carric of Paredocks, Final Address

player_overview.avoid_if: You want to conquer land quickly and directly, or do not want to manage agendas, Imperial relations, subjects, and a mid-game period of waiting.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Repair the Free City and build Sway first; use diplomacy, subjects, and measured warfare to unite the Luna in the middle game, then meet the conditions to form Pashainé.
player_overview.overview: You begin as Menibór, a Free City in the Empire of Anbennar. The Lilac Wars have just made the Luna Valley pay a price, yet the city remains famous for adventurer guilds, mercenaries, and the lively Loop. Repair the capital, manage the Emperor and neighbours, then build Sway to seek privileges and support from the other cities; gradually weave the loose city-states into an alliance and eventually form Pashainé, opening another mission tree.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy Imperial diplomacy, resource trading, urban economies, mercenaries, and growing through small-state alliances.
signature_features: Use Luna Sway to bargain with the Emperor for protection, trade rights, and city status.
Two Menibór-specific missions turn mercenaries, adventurer guilds, and the Loop into urban advantages.
20 shared Luna River missions take the campaign from post-war survival toward a city-state alliance; the final chapter can lead to Pashainé.
player_overview.tagline: Use adventurer connections and Free City statecraft to keep the Luna cities from being pushed around by great powers.

reasons: Adventurer guilds, mercenaries, and the Loop give the Free City a strong local identity.
Sway lets a small country leverage the Emperor and agendas into political reach beyond its territory.
The shared missions naturally lead from post-war survival into the long Pashainé formation route.
warnings: A55 has only 2 additional Menibór-specific missions; the other 20 are shared with several Luna countries.
Sway and the city-state alliance require repeated management of agendas, subjects, and attitudes.
Forming B59 switches the mission tree; its successor content should not be counted as A55's direct missions.

values.rationale: Protecting Free City autonomy, preventing cities from becoming great-power pawns, open education, and cross-city negotiation are positive institutions; subjects and limited warfare reduce restraint without changing the public-city political core.
